detailed_rationale:
Borosil Renewables is India's largest maker of low-iron textured solar glass (>15% domestic share, and the world's largest solar-glass producer outside China), a business that has swung from a genuinely troubled multi-year stretch to a sharp recent inflection. The quant sheet's low quality_score (7.44) and modest 3-year ROE reflect real history - FY24-25 included multiple loss-making quarters, driven substantially by the European subsidiary (GMB, Germany), which the company has since exited via insolvency proceedings, citing weak European demand and Chinese underselling. That exit, combined with provisional anti-dumping duty imposed by the Indian government on solar glass imports from China and Vietnam (notified December), has re-rated the domestic business: the latest reported quarter (Jun 2026) posted sales of Rs 406cr, PAT of Rs 87cr and an OPM of 31%, versus a full FY26 (Mar 2026) of Rs 1,556cr sales / Rs 127cr PAT / 28% OPM - a materially better run-rate than the trailing 3-year average the quant model is scoring off, which is exactly why the CSV's stale ROE/ROCE readings look weaker than the business's current trajectory.

Management has approved a Rs 950cr capacity expansion at the Gujarat facility, taking capacity from 1,000 TPD to 1,500 TPD (+50%), with a stated ambition of reaching 60% domestic market share - a direct bet on India's renewable buildout requiring much more domestically-made solar glass, protected from Chinese oversupply by the new duty. Debt has been reduced (to ~Rs 162cr from Rs 252cr) alongside this, and 12.52 lakh shares were allotted on warrant conversion - a modest, already-anticipated dilution rather than a surprise. The stock has re-rated to ~5.18x book value and ~21x trailing earnings, which is a rich multiple relative to the company's actual multi-year track record, even if the current quarter run-rate justifies it.

The risk that has to be underwritten honestly is that this thesis leans heavily on policy support (anti-dumping duty is typically reviewed/renewed periodically, not permanent) layered on a company whose own operating history, ex-duty-protection, has been inconsistent - working capital also looks stretched (inventory days reported around 115 in Mar 2026). Promoter holding has drifted down over the years (from ~74% in 2017 to ~58.8% now), which is a longer-run dilution trend to be aware of even if not itself alarming.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold on both windows and that is the right call here too: growth_3y_score is strong (72.6) and the recent quarter shows a real margin and profitability inflection, but quality_score remains at the bottom of the universe (7.44) reflecting genuinely volatile multi-year history, and the current valuation (5.18x book, ~21x earnings) already prices in a good chunk of the anti-dumping-duty tailwind continuing. Not a rescue candidate (quant already says Hold) and not a case for escalation - the tension between strong recent momentum and weak historical quality is exactly what a Hold call is meant to express.
summary: Borosil Renewables makes solar glass for India's booming renewables sector and has recently turned a corner: it exited a loss-making German unit, benefits from a new anti-dumping duty on Chinese and Vietnamese solar glass, and has approved a 50% capacity expansion in Gujarat. The most recent quarter was genuinely strong (31% operating margin), but this follows several inconsistent, loss-making years, and the stock has already re-rated to reflect the improvement. We rate it a Hold: real tailwinds, but a valuation that now assumes the good times continue and a policy (anti-dumping duty) that is not guaranteed to stay in place indefinitely.
positive_para: The setup is genuinely attractive: India's solar buildout needs domestically-made glass, Borosil is the domestic scale leader, a fresh anti-dumping duty blocks the Chinese/Vietnamese oversupply that had been pressuring pricing, and the company has both cleaned up its balance sheet (exiting the loss-making German subsidiary, cutting debt) and committed capital (Rs 950cr) to a 50% capacity expansion aimed at 60% market share. The most recent quarter's 31% operating margin shows this is already translating into real profitability, not just a narrative.
negative_para: The honest bear case is that a meaningful part of this re-rating rests on a government anti-dumping duty that is periodically reviewed and not a permanent structural moat - if it is diluted, delayed in renewal, or circumvented by Chinese exporters routing through third countries, the pricing power underpinning the recent margin jump could compress quickly. Layered on that policy dependency is a company whose own multi-year operating record (ex-duty-protection, ex-recent-quarter) has been genuinely weak - multiple loss-making quarters in FY24-25 and a quality_score at the bottom of the coverage universe - and working capital (inventory days ~115) is not yet tight. Paying ~5.18x book and ~21x earnings assumes the current inflection is durable rather than cyclical.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~21x trailing earnings and ~5.2x book, the market is pricing sustained continuation of the post-duty, post-GMB-exit margin structure plus successful execution of the 50% capacity expansion - a reasonable bet given the visible India solar demand pipeline, but not a cheap one given the company's genuinely inconsistent multi-year history before this inflection. This is a fair-to-somewhat-rich valuation that requires the anti-dumping duty and capacity ramp to both go right; it is not a case clean enough to call undervalued.
